analysis_summaries: This repository contains a single-image sanity-test application for a YOLO11s-Pose ONNX model. It preprocesses an image with RGB letterboxing to 640×640, then runs the model and decodes person boxes and 17 COCO keypoints with NMS. The script can draw poses and uses a simple orientation heuristic to estimate fall-like posture from one still image; that heuristic is not a trained fall classifier. The provided task input is a video file, but the application is documented as single-image-only and does not establish video-frame or timestamp handling.

info.user_prompt:
Build a real-time human pose estimation pipeline for fall detection.

Input: a video file at /home/dread/videos/fall_test.mp4 for now (later the live camera).
Model: a 2D human pose estimation model that outputs the 17 COCO body keypoints
(nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles) with a
confidence score per keypoint, plus a person bounding box. Pick a small or
medium model: the GPU is a GeForce GTX 1650 with 4 GB memory.
Compile the model to a TensorRT FP16 engine (an INT8 engine as well if possible,
for comparison) and give the speed report.

Output: for every frame, write one JSON line to /home/dread/pipegen_out/keypoints.jsonl
containing the frame timestamp in seconds, and for each detected person their id,
bounding box and the 17 keypoints as [x, y, confidence] in pixel coordinates.
Also show the video with the skeleton drawn on it.
Blur the person before saving any frame.

input_roles.input1: video file for now (later the live camera)

evidence: The view holds still between frames, so the camera looks fixed.

said.blur_people: Blur the person before saving any frame.

inputs.role: video file for now (later the live camera)

special_algorithms.description: Assign person IDs across frames for the per-person output and fall detection.
special_algorithms.name: person tracking

special_algorithms.description: Detect falls using the human pose estimates and tracked people. Fall condition: hip drop faster than 1.2 torso lengths per second, followed within 1.5 seconds by the torso remaining more than 60 degrees from vertical while the hip midpoint is less than 0.5 torso lengths above the floor line, held for 3 seconds. For each person, estimate the floor line from the lowest ankle y-position observed while they stand upright during the first 3 seconds of the video.
special_algorithms.name: fall detection

rules.floor_line: lowest ankle y-position while the person stands upright during the first 3 seconds
rules.name: Tilted posture and hips near floor

special_algorithms.condition: Every frame, on the boxes its source task finds; after the model and before every picture output.
special_algorithms.description: Pixelates every person the model finds. Added because input1 must not show people in saved or sent pictures.
special_algorithms.name: People blur

tasks.details: Estimate 2D human pose with the 17 COCO body keypoints (nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles), a confidence score per keypoint, and a person bounding box. Emit keypoint coordinates as [x, y, confidence] in pixels, with frame timestamps in seconds. Use a small or medium model suitable for the named GPU. Blur the person before saving any frame.
Assign person IDs across frames for the per-person output and fall detection.

Detect falls for tracked people using the pose estimates. A fall requires a hip drop faster than 1.2 torso lengths per second, followed within 1.5 seconds by the torso staying more than 60 degrees from vertical while the hip midpoint is less than 0.5 torso lengths above the floor line, held for 3 seconds. Determine the floor line for each person from the lowest ankle y-position observed while that person stands upright during the first 3 seconds of the video.

rules.name: Tilted posture and hips near floor

params.floor_line: lowest ankle y-position while the person stands upright during the first 3 seconds

pipeline_requirements.user_intent_summary: Estimate and track 2D human poses in the supplied video, detect falls using a custom condition I’ll provide, write per-frame keypoints and IDs to JSONL, and display the video with a skeleton.
